issue_request: FHIR-14076 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for STU3. It asked whether standard FHIR search parameters such as _count or resource search parameters could be used with OperationDefinition invocations. The accepted resolution was to document that standard search parameters are in scope for OperationDefinition.kind = query, while servers do not need to support them unless explicitly documented; for OperationDefinition.kind = operation, parameters must be explicitly defined.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 0ce8de7c02663f8bdd2b7865985be9ec6550abb7, svn revision 14271, applied the issue by splitting OperationDefinition narrative into separate Executing Operations and Executing Named Queries sections and adding the original named-query standard-search-parameter sentence.
additional_context: Later Published named-query issues refine the original wording. FHIR-31491 clarified inherited standard/resource search-parameter scope, server-support, CapabilityStatement, and documentation expectations, and its reconciliation commit ac2ee46c80a89b04cdaadb2f8de51eea25c24ca8 is already on the combined branch. FHIR-39318 clarified named-query execution semantics and stale OperationDefinition comments, and its reconciliation commit f86d508e0db21179850573fc570b98303db8a557 is also already on the combined branch. source/fhir.ini actively lists operationdefinition=OperationDefinition, and publish.ini lists search.html.
